nodes.title: Follow-through after a call (blueprint 6.3 v1): a rule (followthrough.rule.set, A2, one approval bound to the template's version, its daily limit and the most it can spend a day on the card) sends an approved utility template when a call of an agent or campaign ends with an outcome or reason code, when the caller asked for WhatsApp, or when a campaign attempt is not answered. A job (channels.followthrough, every 30 s) acts on each call once: the run row is written before the send, so a crash never sends twice; two unanswered attempts give one note per person per rule a day
nodes.rationale: The system actor cannot run an external tool without a card (A3 is a closed list), so the per-send work is a job behind a rule a person approved, as a campaign launch approves many calls. Every send still goes through gatedSend (opt-in, window, door, 2 a day per person, wallet and caps). Marketing templates are refused for rules. Values bind like call-ticket facts: the contact's record or the attempt's variables, never free text; a value past its attribute max age is not used; the bound values are the door's facts, so an amount on the record may be stated and any other may not.
nodes.reverse_if: Buyers need a per-send approval for some purpose (then add an A2 queue for that rule), or the 48-hour look-back misses follow-ups when analysis is slow (then key on analysis completion).

nodes.title: "WhatsApp pe bhej do" on a call is the caller's WhatsApp opt-in for follow-ups (consent purpose follow_up, source in_call, their exact words and the turn as evidence); "WhatsApp mat bhejo" on a call is a WhatsApp opt-out. Read once per finished call (channel_call_read). A general WhatsApp yes never covers marketing: marketing needs a consent row for purpose 'marketing' itself
nodes.rationale: Blueprint 4.11 case table: 'WhatsApp pe bhej do' sets the channel preference and follows up there if opted in. The phrase matcher has look-alike negatives in tests ("WhatsApp mat bhejo", "I am not on WhatsApp", "send it by email").
nodes.reverse_if: Counsel (KC8) says a spoken request on a call is not consent for a WhatsApp message (then it becomes a preference only and a template asks to confirm), or the matcher misreads more than 1 in 50 real caller lines.

nodes.title: A WhatsApp template meets the reply door as its category: utility as a service message (RD7 keeps offers out, which is also Meta's rule for utility), marketing as promotional. A template is fixed text, so any door verdict but pass blocks it, at drafting (on its samples) and at every send (on the bound values)
nodes.rationale: Probed on 2026-10-24: 'enjoy 20% off cleaning this Diwali' is blocked by RD7 in service and passes as promotional.
nodes.reverse_if: Meta's category rules and RD7 disagree on real templates (then Meta's review decides and the door only adds RD4/RD5/RD6).

nodes.title: The reply door passes 'Please reply with the OTP sent to your phone.' (RD4 catches 'share the OTP'). Found while testing WhatsApp templates; for the safety builder
nodes.closes_when: rules.json RD4 catches 'reply with the OTP' (and a cases.json vector holds it in TS and Python), or the safety builder says it is out of scope.

nodes.title: The agents' in-call tool send_whatsapp_link (risk external) is not yet routed to the channels gate; today follow-ups go out after the call through follow-through rules only
nodes.closes_when: The runtime's tool event for send_whatsapp_link reaches gatedSend with an approved template, or the agents owner retires the tool in favour of follow-through rules.
